product.amstrad-pc5286.summary: Compact 16 MHz 80286 with integrated C&T VGA and an optional AdLib-compatible Games Pack.
product.amstrad-pc5286.history: Introduced in 1991, the PC5286 paired a 16 MHz 80286 with one megabyte of RAM, integrated VGA and either floppy-only or 40 MB IDE storage. The Games Pack added Amstrad's AdLib-compatible card, speakers, an AJ-5 joystick and three games. BluMach uses the preserved AM52V004 and C&T Version 220 firmware locally.
product.amstrad-pc5286.warning: Experimental model: POST, Setup, all documented RAM populations, VGA diagnostics, BIOS modes 63h/64h and LIM 4.0 EMS pass. The exact KBC, factory hard-disk geometry, Games Pack card/game port and physical advanced-video timing remain approximations or pending.
Floppy model — no hard disk or sound card
Games Pack — 40 MB IDE and AdLib-compatible sound
product.amstrad-pc5286.creation.note: Internal VGA and all listed RAM populations are validated. The 40 MB image uses a period-compatible CP346 geometry because the exact factory drive is not identified. Games Pack sound uses generic AdLib emulation; its integrated game port is not yet modeled.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.market: Documented in UK material from August–October 1991; an Australian owner reports purchase in 1992. Games Pack price: £899 excluding VAT (£1,056.33 including VAT) in October 1991.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.commerc: Single 1.44 MB floppy without hard disk; floppy plus 40 MB IDE; Games Pack with 40 MB IDE, sound card and game accessories. One megabyte was standard, with 2 MB and 4 MB expansions documented.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.accesso: Games Pack: Amstrad AdLib-compatible ISA card, two speakers, AJ-5 analogue joystick, Links, F-15 Strike Eagle II and Prince of Persia.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.cpu: Intel 80286 at 16 MHz, AT bus and optional 80287 socket.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.memory: Paired 80 ns SIMMs: 1, 2 or 4 MB commercial populations. BluMach also supports the manual's 512 KB map but does not present it as a sold configuration.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.chipset: Owner-reported C&T F82C235-12 and F82C710A. SCAT version 04h and memory/EMS behavior are observed; exact board schematics and KBC firmware are unavailable.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.video: Integrated C&T F82C452 with ADV476KP35E RAMDAC and 256 KiB VRAM observed on the MC0128A board. Standard VGA, BIOS 720×540×16 and 800×600×16, advanced registers and an experimental graphics cursor are modeled.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.storage: One 1.44 MB floppy and optional 40 MB IDE. BluMach uses generic ISA IDE and a CP346-compatible 805/4/26 geometry for creation; the exact factory drive remains unknown.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.interfa: F82C710-compatible serial, parallel and floppy functions; generic AT keyboard controller and mouse path remain compatible approximations.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.firmwar: AM52V004 64 KiB system BIOS and C&T Version 220 32 KiB VGA BIOS. Local files are required and checked against recorded hashes; firmware is not distributed.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.verifie: Cold POST and reset recovery, Setup save, 1/2/4 MB memory reporting, SCAT shadow/remap, direct EMS, SCATEMM 1.4 LIM 4.0, standard VGA, BIOS modes 63h/64h and guest graphics cursor demonstration.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.limitat: Experimental. Generic AT KBC/NVR and ISA IDE are substitutes. Games Pack uses the generic AdLib device without the Amstrad card's game port. Advanced C&T timings, frame IRQ, external sync and physical cursor behavior need hardware comparison.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.brochur: Amstrad PC5286 Games Pack brochure and contemporary commercial material.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.manual: PC5086/PC5286 User Instructions; the service manual remains missing.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.firmwar: FreddyV system/VGA dumps published by Banjo; exact hashes and provenance are recorded in the private preservation manifest.
product.amstrad-pc5286.technical.sound_c: Independent restoration of Amstrad 3100-015P-4 confirms a YM3812-class AdLib clone with integrated game port; photographed PC5286 evidence also shows a 3100-015P-3 marking.
